meta_description: Check your bag against the official cabin baggage limits of European airlines, trains and ferries. Every limit links to the operator's own page and shows the date it was checked.
standfirst: Type your bag's size and see in seconds which airlines, trains and ferries will let it on.
measure_note: Measure the whole bag, including handles and wheels. Change any figure to check yours.
nudge_hint: Nudge a figure with the − and + buttons, the up and down arrow keys, or the scroll wheel while the field is selected, and watch the results move. Hold Shift for tenths.
legend_pass_t: Your bag matches an allowance that is already included in the fare.
legend_paid_t: Your bag matches the cabin bag dimensions, but that cabin bag is not included in the base fare. You have to buy it.
legend_fail_t: Your bag is over the published limit on size, weight, or both.
legend_rule_t: The operator describes what you can bring instead of publishing measurements — common on trains. We show their rule in their own words and never turn it into a yes or no.
legend_unknown_t: The operator doesn't publish what we'd need to answer. A missing limit is not the same as no limit.
h3_wheels: Handles and wheels change the answer
p_wheels: Some operators measure your bag with handles and wheels included; others measure the bag body and allow the wheels to stick out by a set number of centimetres. A bag labelled 55 cm can measure 58 cm in the sizer. Where an operator publishes which basis it uses, we say so on the result. Where it doesn't, we say that too.
h3_sourced: Every limit is sourced and dated
p_sourced: Each result links to the operator's own page and shows the date a human opened that page and confirmed it. We don't copy limits from blogs or luggage brands, because that is how out-of-date measurements spread.
h3_noguarantee: Fitting the rules is not a guarantee
p_noguarantee: Meeting a published limit is not a promise that staff will accept your bag at the gate. At least one operator states that paying at the gate does not guarantee a bag over the limit will be carried.
footer_scope: Willitboard covers cabin baggage: the personal item and the cabin bag. Checked baggage rules differ by operator and by what you buy, so we show them as reference rather than as a verdict.
band_pass_empty: No operator here includes a bag this size in the fare. That is the usual answer for anything bigger than a small underseat bag — and it is exactly what catches people out.
band_paid_empty: No operator here sells an allowance your bag fits.
band_fail_empty: Your bag is within the published limits everywhere we cover.
band_rule_empty: No operator here publishes a written rule instead of measurements.
band_unknown_empty: Nothing here is missing the measurements we'd need.
d_rule: This operator describes what you can bring instead of publishing measurements, so a size check can't produce a yes or no.
d_unknown: This operator doesn't publish the measurements needed to answer. A missing measurement is not the same as no limit.
d_fits: Fits the {label} included in the fare: {dims}{kg}.
d_paid: Fits the {label} dimensions ({dims}{kg}), but that bag is not included in the base fare.
d_maybe: Your bag is {by} over the {label} limit of {dims}.
d_over_both: Over the largest allowance ({dims}) by {by}, and over its {kg} kg weight limit.
d_over_weight: Within the size of the {label} ({dims}), but over its weight limit of {kg} kg.
d_over_dims: Over the largest cabin allowance ({dims}) by {by}.
flag_wheels_included: Published limits already include handles and wheels, so measure your bag as it stands.
flag_wheels_excluded: Published limits exclude handles and wheels.
flag_wheels_excluded_tol: Published limits exclude handles and wheels, and wheels may add at most {tol} cm on top.
flag_wheels_unknown: This operator doesn't publish whether handles and wheels count toward the limit. If your bag is within a couple of centimetres of it, assume they do.
flag_no_weight: No weight limit is published for this allowance. That isn't the same as no limit.
flag_maybe: That limit excludes handles and wheels, and allows the wheels to add up to {tol} cm. Whether your bag complies depends on how much of that excess is wheels. Measure the body of the bag without them to find out.
flag_maybe_addon: Either way, this allowance requires buying {addon}.
axes_legend: One bar per side of your bag, against the limit for that side. Sides are matched longest to longest, because a bag can be turned.
need_dims: Enter all three dimensions to check your bag.
stamp: Dataset {version}, generated {date} — {n} {opword} published. Limits in cm and kg.
load_error: The operator limits could not be loaded, so no result can be shown. Rather than guess, this page shows nothing at all. ({message})
_comment_ficha: Textos de la ficha por operador (template_operator.html). Ningún valor de acá es un dato de equipaje: medidas, condiciones, citas, fuentes y fechas viven en operators.json.
fiche_meta_dim: {name} personal item and cabin bag limits in cm and kg, what the fare includes and what costs extra. Linked to the operator's own page, with the date a human checked it.
fiche_meta_rule: What {name} publishes about luggage, quoted in their own words. Linked to the operator's own page, with the date a human checked it. No invented measurements.
fiche_standfirst_dim: What {name} publishes for the personal item and the cabin bag, what the fare already includes, and what has to be bought separately. Every figure on this page comes from the operator's own page.
fiche_standfirst_rule: {name} describes what you can bring instead of publishing measurements. Their rule is shown below in their own words, and never turned into a yes or no.
allow_no_kg: No weight limit published. That is not the same as no limit.
allow_not_published: {name} doesn't publish measurements for this allowance. A missing measurement is not the same as no limit.
caveat_missing: An empty field on this page means the operator doesn't publish that figure. It never means there is no limit.
caveat_fares: Operators sell several fares, and what is included can differ between them. The source link above goes to the page these figures were read from.
prov_why: Not copied from a blog or a luggage brand.
fiche_cta: Check your own bag against every operator
fiche_stamp: Figures from dataset {version}, generated {date}. Limits in cm and kg.

privacy_meta: Willitboard sets no cookies, runs no analytics and collects nothing about you. What that means in practice, and the one third party involved.
privacy_standfirst: What this site knows about you, in full. The short answer is nothing, and this page explains why that is a fact about how it is built rather than a promise.
cookies_meta: Willitboard sets no cookies and writes nothing to your browser's storage. How to check that yourself in fifteen seconds.
cookies_standfirst: This site sets no cookies at all, which is why you were never shown a consent banner. Here is how to confirm that for yourself.
disclosure_meta: Willitboard carries no advertising, affiliate links or paid placement today, and the rules it commits to for when it does.
disclosure_standfirst: Nothing on this site is paid for. This page says so while that is still true, and sets out the rules that stay fixed once money is involved.
